title: AI literacy, and who is trained
desc: The one Art. 4 attestation in Settings, the competence record per member, and the clock that stops both going stale.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can record your organisation's AI-literacy measures against EU AI Act Art. 4, keep the per-member competence record current, and put the annual re-confirmation on the obligations clock so nobody has to remember it.

steps.title: The question procurement will ask
steps.bodyMd:
Van Dijk Groep is a sixty-person Dutch installation firm. Its engineers let agents draft quotations and summarise site reports. Marieke runs the workspace as organisation admin.

A customer's procurement officer sends one line: *"Under Art. 4 of the AI Act, how do you ensure the people operating these systems are AI-literate?"*

That obligation has applied since **2 February 2025**, and it applies to **deployers** — organisations using AI systems — not only to the companies that build them.

Two places in the Compliance Hub answer it, and they are not the same place:

- the rail row **Settings**, group **AI Act**
- the register **Training & competence**, in the **Registers** group of the rail

Neither of them trains anybody. Both of them record.

steps.title: One date for the organisation, one row per person
steps.bodyMd:
**AI literacy is answered once, for the whole organisation.** It is a single stamp in Compliance → **Settings**: you confirmed that guidelines, briefings or training exist for the people who operate AI here. One date, one actor.

**Competence is answered per member.** Every person in the organisation gets a row under **Training & competence** with what they acknowledged, what they completed, and whether a training attestation stands.

The split follows the two rules underneath. Art. 4 asks what measures *the organisation* took. ISO 27001 control **A.6.3** — awareness, education and training — asks per person.

Both are **attestations** — human declarations with a timestamp, not something the software measured. That is why the Overview reports its score split as **automated / attestation / hybrid** rather than blending the two.

steps.question: Van Dijk Groep gives every engineer a 45-minute briefing on its new AI-use guideline and puts the guideline on the intranet. Which action makes the AI Act Art. 4 check stop warning?

choices.label: In Compliance → Settings, group AI Act, press Confirm measures now and then Save.
Press Attest training on every engineer's row under Training & competence.
choices.feedback: Those rows are the per-person competence record. The Art. 4 check reads one organisation-level field in Settings, so it keeps warning however many rows you attest.

choices.label: Publish the guideline as a policy document so everyone acknowledges it.
choices.feedback: Acknowledgements of a published policy are what the Policies column counts, and publishing is worth doing — but the Art. 4 check never looks at policy acknowledgements; it reads one confirmation date.

choices.label: Nothing — the Learning column rises by itself once people have been briefed.
choices.feedback: That column counts modules completed in the Learning Center. A briefing you gave in a meeting room is invisible to it, and it is not what the Art. 4 check reads.

steps.explanation: Art. 4 is answered by one organisation-level attestation. It lives in Compliance → Settings under the AI Act group, and it only becomes real once the page is saved.

steps.title: Where the attestation is made — and the step people miss
steps.bodyMd:
Rail → **Settings** → group **AI Act**, described as *"AI literacy (Art. 4) and the marking of AI-generated content (Art. 50(2))"*. Inside it sits the block **AI literacy (EU AI Act Art. 4)**, with two things to touch:

- **Training material URL (optional)** — paste the intranet page or the course link.
- a stamp with one button, **Confirm measures now**.

Before anything is confirmed the stamp reads **Not confirmed yet**. Press the button and it reads **Confirmed {date} — remember to save**.

Read that ending again. The button only fills the form. At the bottom of Settings a **Save** button sits in a sticky bar, with **Unsaved changes** beside it while the form differs from what is stored. Navigate away without pressing **Save** and nothing was attested.

steps.question: Marieke pressed Confirm measures now, saw "Confirmed 3 March — remember to save", then went to the Overview and pressed Run now. The check still reports: "No AI-literacy attestation on record." What happened?

choices.label: The stamp only sat in the form; without pressing Save at the bottom of Settings, nothing was stored.
Attestations only take effect at the next automatic sweep, six hours later.
choices.feedback: Run now re-runs the checks immediately against stored state — that is the point of the button. The timing is not the problem; the storing is.

choices.label: The Training material URL is required before a confirmation counts.
choices.feedback: That field is labelled "(optional)". Leaving it empty only means the passing detail line does not add the note that training material is linked.

choices.label: Confirming AI literacy needs the Data Protection Officer role, which she does not hold.
choices.feedback: Organisation Admin, Data Protection Officer and ISMS Internal Auditor all carry the compliance permission. If she could not act, the button would not have been there.

steps.explanation: The stamp writes a date into the form, and the wording says so: "Confirmed {date} — remember to save". The Settings page stores nothing until you press Save.

steps.title: What the check actually does with that date
steps.bodyMd:
The check is called **AI literacy programme**, its home framework is the AI Act, its article is 4, its severity is **medium** and its verification label is **attestation**.

It reads two stored values — the confirmation date and the optional material URL — and then does arithmetic on one number, the age of the date:

- no date at all → **warn**, with the advice to confirm your training measures under Compliance → Settings
- older than **365 days** → **warn**: re-confirm annually, because staff and systems change
- anything newer → **pass**, and the detail line says how many days ago you attested

It never fails, and it never verifies. Medium severity carries weight 1 in the score; a warn counts half a pass, so a stale attestation quietly costs half of its weight in the AI Act score and lands in **Needs attention**.

steps.title: Five things that happened at Van Dijk Groep
steps.instruction: Each of these landed on Marieke's desk this month. Match it to the place in the hub that actually records it.

pairs.left: Every engineer sat through the AI-use briefing and the guideline is now on the intranet.
pairs.right: Settings → AI Act → Confirm measures now
pairs.note: One organisation-level attestation, with the intranet page in Training material URL (optional). This is the only thing the Art. 4 check reads.

pairs.left: Anne spent two days at an external security-awareness course and came back with a certificate.
pairs.note: Per person, under People & competence. Record attestation stores who attested, when, and an optional note naming the course, the provider and the certificate.

pairs.left: Marieke wants to see who has actually read the information-security policy as published.
pairs.right: The Policies column on the member's row
pairs.note: Acknowledgements of the published version, counted by the platform. Nothing to attest — this one is measured.

pairs.left: A new colleague worked through three lessons in the Learning Center in her first week.
pairs.right: The Learning column on the member's row
pairs.note: Platform learning progress, also counted automatically. It says she learned something here, not that she is trained for her job.

pairs.left: Nobody at Van Dijk Groep will remember to redo any of this next March.
pairs.note: The obligations clock on the same page. A repeat interval is what makes the work come back on its own.

steps.title: The competence table is a table of clocks
steps.bodyMd:
Rail → **Training & competence**. The intro line sets the scope: *"Who acknowledged which policy, who was trained, and what the ISMS owes itself next."*

Under **People & competence** each member has four columns: **Member**, **Policies**, **Learning** and **Training valid until**.

That fourth column is the one admins misread. An attestation is good for **twelve months**, and that window *is* the clock: the cell counts down from the day you attested to twelve months later.

Somebody who was never attested reads **Never attested** — no clock, and deliberately not a red one. You cannot be overdue for something nobody ever claimed.

**Attest training** opens a drawer with a **Note** field (*"Optional note — course, provider, certificate…"*) and the button **Record attestation**. Afterwards the row reads **Training attested {date}** with **Re-attest** beside it. The rail row keeps the tally as `{done}/{total}`.

steps.question: Van Dijk Groep confirmed its AI-literacy measures 400 days ago and nothing has been touched since. What does the next run report for the AI literacy programme check?

choices.label: A warning that the attestation is 400 days old and should be re-confirmed annually.
A failure — the attestation has expired, so the check treats it as absent.
choices.feedback: This check has only two outcomes, pass and warn. An ageing attestation is never a red item; it warns exactly as an absent one does.

choices.label: A pass — the confirmation is stored, and a stored date does not expire.
choices.feedback: The check measures the age of the date. Past 365 days it moves to warn, because the staff and the systems in use have probably changed since.

choices.label: Nothing at all — the check is skipped until someone confirms again.
choices.feedback: It is never skipped. It runs on every sweep and reports warn, which puts it into Needs attention and costs half of its weight in the AI Act score.

steps.explanation: Never confirmed and confirmed too long ago produce the same warning, on purpose: both mean nobody can say today that the people operating AI here know what they are doing.

steps.title: The clock that brings the work back
steps.bodyMd:
The second half of the same page is **Obligations & deadlines** — the ISMS clock for recurring work.

**Add obligation** opens a drawer with:

- **Kind** — Policy review, SoA review, Internal audit, Management review, **Training**, Access review, Supplier review, Penetration test, Custom
- **Title**, and **Subject** for a policy slug, control reference or supplier
- **Due date**
- **Repeat (months)** — *"With a repeat interval, completing creates the next occurrence automatically — reminders go out 30, 7 and 0 days before due."*
- **Owner**, which defaults to **No owner**

**Create obligation** puts it on the clock; **Mark done** completes it, after which the row reads **Done {date}**. Give it a repeat interval and completing it immediately creates the next occurrence.

steps.question: Marieke adds "Re-confirm AI literacy" with a due date but leaves Repeat (months) empty. A year later she presses Mark done. What happens next?

choices.label: The row reads Done, nothing new is created, and next year nothing reminds anyone.
A new occurrence appears twelve months out, because the Art. 4 window is a year.
choices.feedback: The roll-forward comes from Repeat (months) on the obligation, not from the check. Without an interval the obligation is a one-off.

choices.label: Completing the obligation also refreshes the AI-literacy stamp in Settings.
choices.feedback: Two separate records. Completing an obligation records the obligation; the attestation date only moves when someone presses Confirm measures now and saves.

choices.label: The reminders keep arriving at 30, 7 and 0 days until someone confirms in Settings.
choices.feedback: Reminders run ahead of a due date, not after it is completed. A finished one-off obligation is simply silent.

steps.explanation: An obligation without a repeat interval fires once. The whole point of putting the annual re-confirmation on the clock is the interval, because the check itself will only start warning after the year has already passed.

steps.title: Your turn: the attestation Van Dijk Groep could defend
steps.instruction: Marieke is about to press Confirm measures now. In four or five sentences, write what she would be declaring: which AI-literacy measures actually exist at Van Dijk Groep, who they cover, where the material lives (what she would paste into Training material URL), and how the re-confirmation is scheduled so it is not forgotten. Be concrete about the organisation, not about the regulation — a strong answer names real measures, real people and a real date, and is honest about what the attestation does not prove.
steps.placeholder: e.g. Everyone who uses an agent at Van Dijk Groep — 38 of our 60 people — went through a 45-minute briefing on what the tools may and may not be given…

steps.title: Put the annual re-confirmation on the clock
steps.instruction: Open Training & competence and press Add obligation. Set Kind to Training, give it a title your successor would understand, pick a due date, set Repeat (months) to 12 and choose an owner — then press Create obligation. This is a planning act, not an attestation: you are scheduling the work, not declaring it done.

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Answer the Art. 4 question.** Compliance → Settings → group **AI Act**: paste the material link, press **Confirm measures now**, and then press **Save** — the stamp says *remember to save* because the button alone stores nothing.
- **Read the check honestly.** **AI literacy programme** is medium severity and labelled **attestation**: no date warns, a date over 365 days old warns, anything newer passes. It records a declaration; it never verifies that training happened.
- **Keep the competence table current.** **Member · Policies · Learning · Training valid until**, with **Never attested** where no one has declared anything, and **Attest training** → **Record attestation** for courses taken outside the platform, valid twelve months.
- **Make next year automatic.** An obligation of kind **Training** with **Repeat (months)** set brings the re-confirmation back on its own, with reminders 30, 7 and 0 days before it is due.

Everything here is reversible: a confirmation can be re-made, an attestation re-attested, an obligation completed or left.

ex-compliance-training-and-literacy-meas.title: A defensible AI-literacy attestation
ex-compliance-training-and-literacy-meas.task: Write, in four or five sentences, what Van Dijk Groep would be declaring when it presses Confirm measures now: the measures that exist, who they cover, what goes into Training material URL, and how the annual re-confirmation is scheduled.
criteria: Names at least one concrete measure (a briefing, a written AI-use guideline, an induction step, a course) rather than repeating the words of Art. 4.
Says who the measures cover — the people who actually operate the AI systems — and does not silently claim the whole company if only part of it was trained.
Points at something that could go in Training material URL (optional): an intranet page, a guideline document or a course link.
Schedules the re-confirmation within a year, ideally as a recurring Training obligation with Repeat (months), because the check warns once the date passes 365 days.
Shows awareness that this is an attestation: a declaration with a date and an actor, not proof that anyone learned anything.
ex-compliance-training-and-literacy-meas.guidance: Pass a concrete, modest answer. Do not pass an answer that only paraphrases the AI Act, that claims a measure the learner has not described ("we are fully compliant", "all staff are certified") with nothing behind it, that confuses this organisation-level attestation with per-person Attest training, or that treats the confirmation as permanent with no plan to renew it.

practiceTopic.title: AI literacy and the competence record
practiceTopic.summary: How EU AI Act Art. 4 is attested for the organisation, how per-member competence is recorded, and how the obligations clock keeps both from going stale.
facts: The AI-literacy attestation lives in Compliance → Settings, group AI Act: the field Training material URL (optional) and the stamp AI literacy (EU AI Act Art. 4) with the button Confirm measures now.
Confirm measures now only fills the form — the stamp then reads "Confirmed {date} — remember to save", and nothing is stored until the Save button at the bottom of Settings is pressed.

The check AI literacy programme is medium severity with the verification label attestation: it warns when nothing is confirmed, warns again once the confirmation is older than 365 days, and otherwise passes.
Training & competence shows Member, Policies, Learning and Training valid until per member; someone with no attestation reads Never attested, and the rail row shows {done}/{total}.

Attest training opens a Note field ("Optional note — course, provider, certificate…") and Record attestation; the row then reads Training attested {date} with Re-attest, and an attestation is valid twelve months.
Obligations & deadlines on the same page: Add obligation takes Kind, Title, Subject, Due date, Repeat (months) and Owner, and Create obligation puts it on the clock.
With a repeat interval, completing an obligation with Mark done creates the next occurrence automatically, and reminders go out 30, 7 and 0 days before the due date.
Obligation kinds are Policy review, SoA review, Internal audit, Management review, Training, Access review, Supplier review, Penetration test and Custom.

actionChecks.label: Put a recurring obligation on the clock
actionChecks.hint: In Settings → Compliance → Training & competence, press Add obligation, set Kind to Training and Repeat (months) to 12, then Create obligation.

endpoints.returns: { personnel[{user_id, displayName, email, policy_acks, policy_total, learning_done, attested_at, attested_note}], obligations[{id, kind, title, subject, due_at, recur_months, owner_user_id, completed_at}] }

criteria.label: At least one obligation is on the clock
criteria.hint: Press Add obligation on the Training & competence page, fill in a title and a due date, and press Create obligation. Set Repeat (months) to 12 as well — the recurrence is stored on the row, not visible here.
criteria.rule: GET /api/compliance/iso/training → obligations is a non-empty array (personnel is NOT usable: every org has members)
